changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 2.0.10[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]Real-Debrid[/COLOR]
-Real-Debrid plays again. Since 15 October, Debrid Media Manager only answers its own website when asked which torrents Real-Debrid has cached, and refuses add-ons. luc_kodi used that answer to keep only cached torrents, so with no answer it dropped every Real-Debrid result: the search found sources and "No stream available" came up straight away.
-Without that answer, Real-Debrid torrents are listed as unchecked and checked when you play them: one that is not cached is removed from your account at once and the next source plays.
-DMM sponsors can enter their own key in Accounts > Real-Debrid > DMM API key. With it, luc_kodi asks DMM's sponsor API and shows cached and uncached torrents as before. A key DMM refuses is reported once and playback carries on as unchecked.
-When DMM has not seen any of the torrents cached, they are now listed as unchecked instead of hidden: a torrent DMM has not seen can still be cached.
-Only Real-Debrid changes. TorBox and Premiumize keep checking their own cache, AllDebrid resolves when you play as it always did, and Torrentio, Comet, MediaFusion and AIOStreams with your Real-Debrid key still bring their own cached results. The DMM scraper keeps searching as before.
[COLOR fffdb515]Fixes[/COLOR]
-Exported logs now also blank out the PunchPlay and WeTrakr tokens, the MDBList refresh token, the TMDb password and session, your personal TheTVDB key and PIN, the old Meteor address (it carries the config token) and the new DMM key. They came after the log export was written and had been left out.
-TorrentsDB no longer writes an error to the log on every search its server does not answer. No answer just means no results, as it already did for season packs.
-AIOStreams switched on but not set up writes a warning in the log instead of an error with an empty trace.
-TV shows that ended or were cancelled count their aired episodes like the ones still running, leaving out specials and episodes that never aired. A check that could never match made it work by accident; it is now done on purpose, and TMDb's total number of episodes is only used when TMDb does not say which episode aired last.
